propositions: A new read-only `rebar bridge suggest-mapping <PROJECT>` command observes a live Jira project and emits a suggested `[tool.rebar.mapping]` config block seeded with discovered vocabulary and identity-seed axis maps.

The probe grounds all axes using high-level pycontribs `jira.JIRA` public methods: `issue_types()`, `priorities()`, `issue_link_types()`, `statuses()`, `createmeta_issuetypes()`, and `search_issues()` + `transitions()` for partial transition hints.

The `--write` flag performs deep-merge into an existing `rebar.toml` or creates one, preserving flat `[jira]` and `[tracker]` sections, with existing mapping keys winning; `pyproject.toml` is never edited.
Two new serialization helpers `_emit_nested_toml` and `_emit_config_toml` orchestrate writing the nested `[mapping.*]` structure while the existing `_emit_toml` remains untouched on flat sections.
The probe is fully offline via a fake port in unit tests; transition data is marked best-effort/partial because only the current status's transitions are discovered per sample issue.
Comments in `[mapping]` blocks are not preserved during merge due to `tomllib` limitations, but existing hand-edited values are retained and never clobbered.
